Computer Numerically Controlled Tool Operators run CNC lathes, mills, and machining centers. They clamp workpieces, set tools, monitor cycles, read measuring instruments and dimensional reports, respond to tool wear and exceptions, and keep production parts within drawing tolerances.

paragraphs: A shift begins by checking the drawing and machining program. The operator clamps the first piece, sets the tools, performs a dry run and test cut, and measures the result before automatic production. During the run, chip color and sound reveal problems, and dimensional drift triggers an offset adjustment. A batch change requires cleaning and a new setup. Before leaving, the operator clears chips, inspects the machine, updates the log, and retains the first-piece sample.

CNC operation suits people who combine sustained focus, numerical awareness, and a drive for precision. You need to read drawings, set offsets accurately, and keep every part within tolerance.

This career rewards an intense focus on precision. A ±0.01 tolerance on a drawing is not decoration; exceeding it can scrap a batch. It suits people who can stay focused, read numbers quickly, scrutinize measurements, and work well around oil odors and noise.
